topic.subject: social
topic.title: Agriculture
topic.scope: types of farming, cropping seasons, major crops, food security, technological and institutional reforms

nodes.name: Use of HYV seeds and fertilizers

misconceptions.statement: Primitive farming is only practiced by tribal people in remote forests.
misconceptions.why: Students associate 'primitive' with 'tribal' due to media stereotypes.
misconceptions.fix: It is a method of cultivation based on natural environmental conditions and family labor, not defined by the ethnicity of the farmer.

probe.question: Can a farmer in a non-tribal village practice primitive subsistence farming?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because they are not tribal.

misconceptions.root_belief: Labels define the nature of an activity.

misconceptions.statement: Rabi crops are grown in summer because they need a lot of heat.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the harvest time (summer) with the growing time.
misconceptions.fix: Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in summer; they require cool weather for germination and warm weather for maturation.

probe.question: When are wheat seeds sown?
probe.wrong_answer: In the summer, because it is a Rabi crop.

misconceptions.root_belief: Harvest time is the same as growing time.

misconceptions.statement: MSP is the price at which the government sells food to the poor.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the procurement price (MSP) with the issue price (PDS).
misconceptions.fix: MSP is the price at which the government buys crops from farmers to ensure they get a fair return.
misconceptions.root_belief: Government schemes always involve selling to the public.

misconceptions.statement: Using more fertilizers always leads to higher crop yields indefinitely.
misconceptions.why: Students apply a linear 'more is better' logic without considering soil health.
misconceptions.fix: Excessive use of fertilizers degrades soil quality and reduces fertility over time, leading to lower yields in the long run.

probe.question: What happens if a farmer doubles the recommended fertilizer dose?
probe.wrong_answer: The crop will grow twice as fast and yield more.

misconceptions.root_belief: Bigger or more means more effect.

misconceptions.statement: Intensive subsistence farming means using lots of machines and big farms to grow crops for sale.
misconceptions.why: Students read 'intensive' as 'industrial' and link it with mechanisation and large scale.
misconceptions.fix: Intensive subsistence farming is done on small plots using lots of labour and farm inputs to get high output per unit of land, mainly to feed the farmer's family.

probe.question: A farmer in a crowded part of the Ganga plain works a tiny plot with family labour and grows rice for his family. Which type of farming is this?
probe.wrong_answer: Commercial farming, because the work is very intensive.

misconceptions.statement: Commercial farming means farmers do not grow food crops like rice or wheat.
misconceptions.why: Students link commercial farming only with cash crops like tea and cotton.
misconceptions.fix: Commercial farming means crops are grown mainly for sale; the crop can be rice or wheat too, as in Punjab and Haryana, where the commercialisation level is high.

probe.question: Rice is grown for sale in Punjab and Haryana on a large scale. What type of farming is it?
probe.wrong_answer: Subsistence farming, because rice is a food crop.

misconceptions.root_belief: Crop type decides farming type, not purpose

misconceptions.statement: Zaid crops are grown in the same season as Kharif crops, in the monsoon.
misconceptions.why: Students remember Zaid as a 'summer-ish' season and mix it with the rainy season.
misconceptions.fix: Zaid is a short season between Rabi and Kharif, in summer (March to June), with crops like watermelon, cucumber and fodder. Kharif starts with the monsoon in June–July.

probe.question: In which season are watermelon and cucumber mainly grown in India?

misconceptions.root_belief: Zaid is the same as Kharif

misconceptions.statement: Food security just means that a country grows enough food in total.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on national production and ignore access and affordability.
misconceptions.fix: Food security means all people have availability, access and affordability of food at all times. Enough production does not help if poor people cannot buy it.

probe.question: India has big food grain stocks, yet some poor people still sleep hungry. Is India food secure?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because food is available in the country.

misconceptions.root_belief: Food security equals total food production
misconceptions.source_hint: NCERT Class 9 Economics / FAO definition studies

misconceptions.statement: Slash and burn farming is done on the same plot every year.
misconceptions.why: Students picture a fixed field and do not see the shifting cycle.
misconceptions.fix: Farmers clear and burn a patch, grow crops for a few years, then abandon it when soil fertility falls and move to a new patch. This is also called shifting agriculture.

probe.question: After a few harvests on a burnt patch, what does the slash and burn farmer do?
probe.wrong_answer: Adds fertilizer and continues farming on the same patch.

misconceptions.root_belief: All farming uses permanent fixed fields

misconceptions.statement: High population pressure on land is the reason farms in India are large.
misconceptions.why: Students think more people means more land taken up for farming.
misconceptions.fix: Land is limited, so more people means each family's plot gets divided into smaller holdings through inheritance. Small holdings lead to intensive farming.

probe.question: In densely populated areas, what happens to the size of farm holdings over generations?
probe.wrong_answer: They become larger because more people need more food.

misconceptions.statement: HYV seeds give high yields on their own without needing irrigation or other inputs.
misconceptions.why: The name 'high yielding' suggests the seed alone does everything.
misconceptions.fix: HYV seeds give high yields only with assured irrigation, fertilizers and pesticides. This package is why the Green Revolution worked best in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

probe.question: A farmer sows HYV wheat in a dry field without irrigation or fertilizers. What happens to the yield?
probe.wrong_answer: It will still be very high because the seed is high yielding.

misconceptions.root_belief: Improved seeds alone guarantee high yield
misconceptions.source_hint: NCERT Class 10 Geography / Green Revolution case studies

misconceptions.statement: Land reform acts took land from all farmers and gave it to the government.
misconceptions.why: Students mix land reform with land acquisition or collectivisation.
misconceptions.fix: Land reforms such as abolition of zamindari and land ceiling aimed to take surplus land from big landlords and give it to tenants and landless farmers, and to remove middlemen.

probe.question: Who received the surplus land taken from big landlords under land ceiling laws?
probe.wrong_answer: The government kept it all as state farms.

misconceptions.root_belief: Land reform means state takes all private land
